label: thm:rel_upper
title: Linear-condition-number relaxation time of fixed-step ideal Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
work: Optimal Convergence Rate of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for Strongly Logconcave Distributions
difficulty_reason: The fixed-step linear-condition-number relaxation bound requires a synchronous Hamiltonian coupling under strong convexity and gradient Lipschitzness, without the twice-differentiability assumed in earlier estimates. The authors retain the time-dependent curvature in both the position and velocity bounds and integrate its monotone accumulation to obtain the sharp contraction scale, a substantive new argument beyond directly applying standard global-Lipschitz ODE stability. The complete crude-bound proof and the precisely cited Ricci-curvature-to-spectral-gap prerequisite are retained.
required_context: Selected Theorem1.3 is the O(kappa) relaxation upper bound for ideal HMC at fixed T=1/(2sqrt(L)), not the distinct lower bound or discretized numerical complexity theorem. Full original mathematical article and bibliography retained conservatively; full paired-position/velocity contraction proof603–740, final spectral-gap reduction742–754, and complete author crude-bound proof761–811. Standard convex-gradient cocoercivity and general Ricci/spectral-gap relation are stated and precisely cited as pre-existing prerequisites. Supporting contraction claim is not an additional unit. The original single illustrative figure is copied byte-identically; approved extensionless alias and compiler-resolved PDF refer to this same single figure.
